Bisher erhaltene Abrechnungen der Leistungserbringer und/oder deren Dienstleistern, die in Papierform eingehen, sollen durch den Auftragnehmer digitalisiert und so der Auftraggeberin zur Verfügung gestellt werden. Dadurch erleichtert sich für die Auftraggeberin die Rechnungs- bearbeitung und es wird Potenzial für Prozessoptimierungen und -automatisierungen geschaf- fen. Details sind der Leistungsbeschreibung zu entnehmen. 1.1 Losbildung Eine Losbildung unterbleibt, da ein ganzheitlicher Scandienst mit der Gesamtverantwortung des künftigen Auftragnehmers ausgeschrieben wird. Ausgeschrieben wird ein Rahmenvertrag mit einem Wirtschaftsteilnehmer. Bieter sind aufgefordert, ein Angebot einzureichen. 1.2 Art der Vergabe Die Auftraggeberin schreibt die benötigten Leistungen in einem offenen Verfahren im Sinne von § 15 VgV aus. Dieses Vergabeverfahren wird aus Gründen der Transparenz über eine elektronische Vergabeplattform betrieben. Die Auftraggeberin verwendet ausschließ lich die Vergabeplattform der DTVP Deutsches Vergabeportal GmbH (www.dtvp.de). Es ist das zum Zeitpunkt der Veröffentlichung der Bekanntmachung geltende Vergaberecht maßgeblich, auch, wenn dieses sich während des Vergabeverfahrens ändern sollte. Form Approved: OMB No. 10670-0052 2 What is the Purpose of Filling out this Form? The Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA) requires each Federal agency to provide security protections for both “information collected or maintained by or on behalf of an agency” and for “information systems used or operated by an agency or by a contractor of an agency or other organization on behalf of an agency.” FISMA and other provisions of Federal law authorize the Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) to promulgate information security standards for information security systems, including to ensure compliance with standards promulgated by the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). Executive Order 14028, “Improving the Nation’s Cybersecurity” (E.O. 14028), emphasizes the importance of securing software used by the Federal Government to perform its critical functions. To further this objective, E.O. 14028 required NIST to issue guidance “identifying practices that enhance the security of the software supply chain.”1 The NIST Secure Software Development Framework (SSDF) (SP 800-218),2 and the NIST Software Suppl

tance. The agency shall take appropriate steps to ensure that the assessment is not posted publicly, either by the vendor or by the agency itself. Additional Information: In the event that an agency cannot obtain a completed self-attestation from the software producer, an agency may still decide to use the producer’s software if the producer identifies the practices to which they cannot attest, documents practices they have in place to mitigate associated risks, and submits a plan of actions and milestones (POA&M) to the agency. f_Work.docx ===== STATEMENT OF WORK (SOW) RFID Cabinet The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Veterans Health Administration (VHA), requires the acquisition of a Radio Frequency Identification (RFID) storage cabinet integrated with Unique Device Identifier (UDI)-compliant tissue and implant tracking software to support patient safety, regulatory compliance, and efficient inventory management. Tracking tissues, biologics, and implantable medical devices is a federal regulatory requirement under FDA 21 CFR Part 830 (UDI) and is critical to patient safety. VA healthcare facilities face ongoing resource challenges including staff shortages and budget constraints, making it essential to minimize staff time consumed by manual data entry and to maintain precise control over high-value inventory. This acquisition will provide an automated, real-time RFID-based inventory management solution for use in the operating room (OR), Catheterization (Cath) lab, ambulatory surgery center, or any facility location that stores high-value implantable inventory. ΤΡΟΠΟΣ ΚΑΙ ΠΡΟΘΕΣΜΙΑ ΥΠΟΒΟΛΗΣ Η προσφορά θα πρέπει να υποβληθεί μέχρι και την Πέμπτη 10 Σεπτεμβρίου 2026 και ώρα 14:00, στην έδρα της ΕΕΑΒΕ Α.Ε., Σωτηρίου Τσερκέζη 20, Ορεστιάδα, Τ.Κ. 68200. . e medical capabilities, austere mission environments, field hospitals and Forward Operating Bases. DoW’s close relationship with the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is paramount. The success of an integrated Federal Electronic Health Record (EHR) is a top national priority. Equally critical is the ability to support the continuum of care across operational and enterprise healthcare environments, ensuring that health information generated during military operations can be captured, exchanged, and made available to support continued care within the enterprise health record. Together, these operational, enterprise, and interagency requirements create a highly complex healthcare ecosystem that includes deployed medical environments, fixed medical treatment facilities, the Federal Health Care Center and other DoW/VA sharing sites. Supporting the ecosystem requires coordinated end user service models and highly configurable enterprise approaches capable of operating across diverse mission environments while enabling interoperability, continuity of care, and interagency collaboration. 1.2 EUS Overview & Transition Strategy To maximize the value of the Department’s health technology investments, PAE MDS is transitioning from legacy, labor-intensive support contracts to a unifie

le DDIL Operations: Ensure training, adoption, and communication resources are available offline and locally to support operational units in Denied, Disrupted, Intermittent, and Limited (DDIL) environments. Maintain a deployable surge capacity to provide short-notice, onsite tactical training, workflow support, and physical setup/teardown of training hardware during military exercises. • Parallel Innovation Framework: Establish a low-risk framework to test, scale, and deploy automated workflows and novel technologies in a live environment without "hard cutovers" that risk clinical downtime. 2.2 Governance, XLAs, Enforcement, & Modern Deliverables Problem Statement: Legacy user-facing services suffer from fragmented governance, static administrative reporting, and unregulated product intake. Standard Service Level Agreements (SLAs) lack financial enforcement linked to actual user satisfaction, making it difficult for the Government to hold vendors accountable for real-world mission outcomes.
